THE FILM THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN READING WITHOUT NAMING
column2: *** 107638608, "WPC PRIVATE GRAVES REGISTERS 1963 - 1970", 488 IMAGES. *** Leonard bought grave 56045 on 13 SEPTEMBER 1969, so folio W 8 is in this film and nowhere else.

column1: and its structure, read from the page
column2: IT IS ALPHABETICAL BY PURCHASER SURNAME. Image 401 is the T section — Theunissen, Tyson, Terblanche, Tennyson, Taljaard, Tomlinson, Taylor, Tommasini, Theron, Thomas, Twogood, Turner. The printed form is numbered 14/6082 and the columns are NAME OF PURCHASER and ADDRESS.

column1: so the folios can be found by arithmetic rather than by luck
column2: T beginning at 401 of 488 puts the letters roughly where an English surname distribution predicts. THE F FOLIOS SHOULD SIT AROUND IMAGES 180 TO 200, AND THE W FOLIOS AROUND 440 TO 470.

folio F 3/8, to see what grave it covers and whether the "Transf. P.Fol. F 3/8." in the Remarks column of burial folio W 56 belongs to Wear's row at all. IT WAS NOT READ TODAY. The FamilySearch image viewer kept reverting to its thumbnail grid and the hunt was abandoned rather than padded out.

column1: why that is a fair trade
column2: the transfer line may not even be Wear's — the archive has said from the start that the ruling puts it in row 4's cell but the page curves and it may belong to row 3. The film number and the alphabetical structure are worth more than one more hour of clicking, because they make every future West Park question cheap.

column1: ONE THING WORTH KNOWING FOR ANY FUTURE GRAVE QUESTION
column2: the other 198 films in olib:4148464 cover Braamfontein, Brixton, Randburg, Ferndale, Olifantsvlei and the West Park sections — burial registers, payment records, private graves and "DRM" and "DRC" series. A grave question in Johannesburg now starts with a film list instead of a search box.
